issues.issue: The small line under the decision pills, “five separate decisions – none implies the next,” is low-contrast and small at 720p.
issues.fix: Increase the font size and contrast, or move the point into a larger caption/pill.

issues.issue: The footer disclaimer/credits are too small to read comfortably at 720p.
issues.fix: Keep the critical “illustrative, not a live AWS run, no real IDs” message in the readable top badge and either enlarge the footer or treat it as non-essential credits.

issues.issue: The subtitle says “From GovTech Golden AMI,” but the required lineage is GovTech/GCC Golden Amazon Linux 2023. This drops “GCC” and “Amazon Linux 2023.”
issues.fix: Change the line to “From GovTech/GCC Golden Amazon Linux 2023 to a trusted DEV → PROD rollout.”

issues.issue: The gray body text in the “GovTech / GCC Golden AMI” card is small and low-contrast at 720p.
issues.fix: Increase size/weight and brighten the body copy, especially “Amazon Linux 2023,” “baseline hardening,” and “some security & operations agents.”

issues.issue: The gray body text in the upstream card remains small and low-contrast at 720p.
issues.fix: Increase the body font size/contrast or simplify the card to the key lineage label.

issues.issue: The bottom subtitle visually collides with the lower-left “never shipped to PROD” callout area, making the frame feel crowded.
issues.fix: Move the callout higher or move the subtitle lower/shorten it so the two elements do not compete.

issues.issue: The GitLab and ECS Worker panels are partially cropped/faded at the left and right edges, including clipped text on the GitLab side.
issues.fix: Reframe or scale the three-panel layout so all panel headings and checks are fully inside the 16:9 safe area.

issues.issue: The left GitLab panel is clipped off-screen, and the MongoDB panel text is dimmed enough to be hard to read at 720p.
issues.fix: Keep all panels within frame, or remove/darken inactive panels further and avoid leaving clipped readable text at the edge.

issues.issue: The MongoDB “PROPOSED” tag sits awkwardly across the boundary between panels.
issues.fix: Keep the tag fully inside the MongoDB card or remove it from this ECS-focused frame.

issues.issue: The frame is visually dense: three validation cards, multiple proposed tags, bottom status chips, and a large subtitle all compete at 720p.
issues.fix: Reduce on-screen copy or split the validation cards and bottom evidence chips across separate shots.

issues.issue: The long “PROD · private launch” line is small for 720p and may be difficult to read, especially the clause about PROD parameters.
issues.fix: Break the line into two larger bullets or increase the font size/weight.

issues.issue: The blocker list says “missing approval or policy,” but Phase B specifically requires management/security/change-governance approval of the policy.
issues.fix: Change to “missing management/security/change-governance approval of policy.”

issues.issue: The blocker list says “missing snapshot or key access,” but the required wording is missing snapshot/KMS access.
issues.fix: Change to “missing snapshot or KMS access.”

issues.issue: The critical vulnerability box says “Ops-approved,” which implies Ops approval alone can authorize an urgent out-of-band release. That conflicts with the rule that Phase B policy requires management/security/change-governance approval.
issues.fix: Change to “approved emergency change under management/security/change-governance policy” or “Ops initiates under pre-approved emergency policy.”

issues.issue: The small explanatory line in the canary rollback box is long and low-contrast at 720p.
issues.fix: Shorten it or enlarge/brighten the text, e.g. “Rollback within approved maintenance window.”

review.overall: Most frames respect the required illustrative/not-live positioning and correctly label proposed EventBridge discovery, MongoDB replica-set gate, and ECS mock/parameter checks. Main accuracy risks are the opening lineage shorthand, Phase B approval wording, KMS wording, and the s37 implication that Ops approval alone is sufficient. Main visual issues are small low-contrast technical text, clipped side panels in the DEV validation sequence, and occasional crowding around subtitles/callouts.
